title: ESO’s ELT home in the desert
caption: The Milky Way over the construction site of the Extremely Large Telescope, Cerro Armazones
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A clear band of the Milky Way frames the excavated summit of Cerro Armazones almost perfectly. The mountaintop, a construction site when this photograph was taken on 5 July 2019, is the home of ESO's Extremely Large Telescope, or ELT.

Cerro Armazones rises to just over 3000 meters above sea level in Chile's Atacama Desert, only 20 km from ESO's Paranal Observatory and its Very Large Telescope. The peak is isolated, far from the light pollution of cities, and that is what makes the Atacama such a good place for observatories. The clear Milky Way in this picture shows how dark the sky is.

The ELT is ESO's upcoming flagship facility, planned to be the world's biggest eye on the sky. Concrete for its foundation began to be poured in December 2019, and at the time of this picture's release the telescope was expected to be finished later in the decade.

understand.summary: This is a night landscape photograph by Petr Horálek. The source gives no camera or color details.
understand.eye: A camera exposure gathers far more starlight than the eye, so the Milky Way looks brighter here than it would to someone on the mountain.
